record.context_brief: from almost complex to integrable complex structures
record.original_question: If a 2n-dimensional manifold admits an almost complex structure, must it also admit an integrable complex structure when n > 2?

evidence.quote: Question 3.21. If \(M^{2n}\) admits an almost complex structure, does it admit an integrable complex structure for \(n>2\)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M^{2n}$ be a smooth closed manifold of real dimension $2n$ with $n>2$. An almost complex structure on $M$ is a smooth bundle endomorphism $J:TM\to TM$ satisfying $J^2=-\mathrm{Id}$. Such a $J$ is called integrable (i.e., comes from a holomorphic atlas making $M$ a complex manifold) if and only if its Nijenhuis tensor
$$N_J(X,Y)=[X,Y]+J[JX,Y]+J[X,JY]-[JX,JY]$$
vanishes identically (Newlander–Nirenberg theorem).

Question: If $M^{2n}$ admits an almost complex structure, must $M^{2n}$ also admit an integrable complex structure (possibly a different one) when $n>2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is widely regarded as open. It coincides with Yau's Problem 52, which conjectures that every compact almost complex manifold of real dimension at least 6 admits an integrable complex structure. The most famous special case—whether the 6-sphere $S^6$ admits a complex structure—remains an unresolved problem in differential geometry.

status_evidence.title: Almost complex manifold - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In higher dimensions, determining whether an almost complex structure can be deformed to an integrable one remains extremely challenging.
status_evidence.claim: The general integrability question in higher dimensions is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Topological aspects of complex and almost complex manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Yau's Problem 52 asserts that every compact almost complex manifold of dimension ≥6 admits a complex structure.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as Yau's Problem 52 and remains an open conjecture.
